newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon property tax revenues slightly down in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon property tax revenues slightly down in Feb.

text.p: Lebanese government revenues from taxation of property deals fell 0.22 percent in February compared to the same month last year, the finance ministry said on Tuesday.
The ministry collected $8.292 million compared with $8.310 million in February 1996, it said in a statement.
Collected revenues for the first two months of 1997 totalled $19.321 million, up from $16.458 million over the same period a year earlier.

Tax rates on property deals vary from district to district, but average about 6.5 percent. However, tax collection does not truly reflect the state of the market because deals are sometimes understated to avoid tax, property analysts said.
